title: Gaps When Everyone Is Free
statement:
You get the calendars of a team: schedules[p] lists the busy blocks of person p as [start, end] pairs. Each person's blocks are sorted by start and do not overlap one another.

Return every stretch of time when nobody on the team is busy, as [start, end] pairs sorted by start. Only count gaps between the first busy moment and the last one (time before everybody starts and after everybody stops is unbounded, so it is left out), and only gaps of positive length: a block ending at 3 and another starting at 3 leave no gap.

examples.why: Together the team is busy during [1, 6], [10, 11] and [13, 15]. The gaps between those blocks are the answer.
The first block ends exactly when the second begins, so there is no free moment of positive length.
The second person has free time between 3 and 5, but the first person is busy then. A gap must be free for everyone.

constraints: Each person has at least one block
hints: Who owns a busy block does not matter for the answer. What happens if you throw all blocks into one list?
You then need the gaps in the union of a set of intervals. Sort by start and merge, the way you would merge overlapping ranges.

While merging, track the furthest end seen so far. Whenever the next block starts strictly after it, [furthest end, next start] is a gap. Since each person's list is already sorted, a heap can merge them without a full sort.

explain.intuition:
A moment is free for everyone exactly when it lies in no busy block of anyone. So forget who owns which block: pour every block into one pile, and the shared free time is the set of holes in the union of the pile.

Holes in a union of intervals come straight out of a sorted sweep. Walk the blocks in order of start time with a running "busy until" mark. A block that starts after the mark opens a gap from the mark to its start; otherwise it only pushes the mark further. Since each calendar is already sorted, you can feed the sweep with a min-heap holding the next block of each person, like merging k sorted lists.
steps: Put the first block of every person into a min-heap keyed by start time.
Set busyUntil to the start of the earliest block.
Pop the earliest block. If its start is greater than busyUntil, record the gap [busyUntil, start]. Then set busyUntil = max(busyUntil, end).
Push that person's next block, if any, and repeat until the heap is empty.
pitfalls: Comparing each block only with the one before it instead of with the furthest end so far. A long block like [1, 10] covers several later ones.
Reporting a zero-length gap when one block ends exactly where the next starts. Use a strict >.
Adding the time before the first block or after the last one. Those stretches are unbounded and not part of the answer.

complexity.time: O(N log k) for N blocks and k people (O(N log N) with a full sort)
complexity.space: O(k) for the heap, plus the output

solutions.title: Flatten, sort and sweep
solutions.idea: Merge all calendars into one list sorted by start, then sweep with the furthest end seen so far.

solutions.title: K-way merge with a min-heap
solutions.idea: Each calendar is already sorted, so a heap holding each person's next block yields all blocks in start order without sorting everything.

followups: Return only the free gaps that are at least d minutes long, and stop after finding the first one.
Find the times when at least m of the k people are free. What do you sweep over instead?
